open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict corpus_digest identity input
open_points.text: M08 introduces “corpus_digest” and says the recorded verdict is for “an implementation and a corpus digest,” but no passage states which corpus facts are inputs to that digest.
open_points.question: From what model facts is corpus_digest minted: only the active TrialCase identities/content, or also TrialCase provenance and record facts such as origin, captured_from, added_by and added_at?
options: Digest only the active TrialCase identities or their identity facts.
Digest the complete persisted TrialCase records, including provenance and addition metadata.
Digest some separately defined corpus snapshot facts.
open_points.default_guess: Digest only the active TrialCase identities, excluding provenance and timestamps.

witness.initial: A contract version has a nonempty corpus containing an authored TrialCase whose identity facts, origin, adding actor and addition time are all stored.
events: An agent submits an implementation when no verdict exists for the current corpus.
The kernel computes and records the corpus_digest in its AdmissionVerdict.
An owner or agent inspects that verdict.
outcomes: An implementation hashing only TrialCase identity facts records one corpus digest.
An implementation hashing the complete TrialCase records records a different corpus digest because origin, actor and time also participate.
witness.observer: An owner or agent inspecting the AdmissionVerdict, and later code using corpus_digest to decide whether a verdict already exists.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: K-05 admission versus M08 AdmissionVerdict and K-02 function execution
set_aside.text: K-05 says “Admission is a deterministic verdict over the whole active corpus,” while K-02 permits code that obtains time or chance by undetected means and says it “is judged by its outputs like any other”; M08 now records the first verdict once and reuses it, “never computed again.”
set_aside.question: Must admission be a repeatable deterministic fact of the implementation and corpus, or may the first observed pass or failure of time- or chance-dependent code become the permanent verdict for that pair?
options: Admission must be repeatable from the implementation and corpus, so implementations capable of time- or chance-dependent results cannot acquire a verdict under the stated deterministic rule.
The first admission executions determine a permanent admitted or refused verdict, even though identical executions at another time could produce the opposite result.
set_aside.default_guess: Treat the first recorded admission result as permanent, because the changed M08 explicitly requires reuse and forbids recomputation.

witness.initial: A contract has one active trial case expecting output 1, and an implementation obtains chance through an undetected mechanism and returns either 1 or 0.
events: An authoring agent submits the implementation.
The kernel executes the active case for admission.
The same implementation is later submitted again against the unchanged corpus.
outcomes: Under K-05's deterministic-fact reading, the implementation cannot validly receive a corpus verdict whose result depends on chance, or admission must otherwise ensure the same result for the pair.

Under changed M08 and K-02, whichever result the first execution produced is recorded permanently: a first 1 admits and activates it, while a first 0 refuses it, and later submissions reuse that result.
witness.observer: The submitting agent and anyone inspecting the implementation's verdict or current activation.
